beats.text: You still check your ex's profile. Most people do!
But it has a price. A study asked four hundred sixty-four people after a breakup how often they checked their ex on Facebook.
The more they checked, the more they longed for their ex. More distress. Less personal growth.
So should you unfriend them? Here's the surprise.
Staying friends wasn't the problem! The checking was.
So the friend list can stay. Just put the phone down.

ask: WHEN DID YOU LAST CHECK? COMMENT.
sources: Lukacs & Quan-Haase (2015), Romantic breakups on Facebook: new scales for studying post-breakup behaviors, digital distress, and surveillance, Information, Communication & Society – 88% of participants said they had 'creeped' an ex-partner after a breakup.

Marshall (2012), Facebook surveillance of former romantic partners: associations with postbreakup recovery and personal growth, Cyberpsychology, Behavior, and Social Networking 15(10) – 464 participants (84% female, mean age 21); more surveillance went with more current distress, negative feelings, sexual desire and longing for the ex and less personal growth; remaining Facebook friends went with fewer negative feelings, less desire and longing (but also lower personal growth); correlational.
